summary: Round 8, scoped to the delta since 87bc946fb5f9. All three of my round-7 minors and the test reviewer's blocker are genuinely closed, and I verified each by mutation in my own tree rather than by reading. (1) The new test theBOUNDEDCrossingStillStopsAtTheSlotTheCONTINUENamed is SOUND and pins the BOUNDED hop specifically: replacing `upTo` with `Long.MAX_VALUE` in `hops.add(new Hop(chainEpoch, checkpoint.sequence(), upTo))` fails exactly one test out of 299, and it is this one; the checkpoint at sequence == barrier is genuinely ACCEPTED (`checkpoint.sequence() - 1 > upTo` is `0 > 1`, false), so the failure proves the bounded hop was taken, not the pre-existing `Hop(chainEpoch, 0, ...)` one. Its own javadoc's second measured claim also checks out: widening all three pre-existing Hop sites fails CommitLogCrossEpochTest.theCrossingStopsAtTheSlotTheCONTINUENamesRatherThanReadingTheWholePredecessor and nothing else. It is not an accidental re-run of the refused-checkpoint sibling. (2) ADR-0035's replacement sentence is TRUE and materially more durable than the census it replaced: I applied the rejected variant (`epoch != ownEpoch && crossFromCheckpoint(...)`) and measured six failures, five of them exact request-count assertions on the bounded path (aCheckpointSittingEXACTLYOnTheBarrierIsUsed 18, aRunOfBURNEDEpochs 14, and the three LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest totals at 17), all of which drop uniformly by one -- so a comparison of two measurements would indeed pass and only exactness catches it. It is a property claim rather than a count of another file's assertions; it can still rot if a future commit turns a bounded-path exact count into an inequality, but that is one level up and the ADR carries the argument against doing so. (3) No production code changed in this delta, so the request-rate lens is unmoved: CheckpointCursor.newest is still one stat plus at most one get per chain probed, the walk still stops at the first hit, and the rate scales with epochs walked, never with records, streams, pods or indices. Suite green at 299 in my tree. One minor, recorded and not blocking: the stale-inventory form does still survive in a test comment, and this delta made it false.

findings.blocks_rationale: review.md `minors-land`: on a pass, a minor is recorded in the commit body and the commit lands, and fixing it is permitted and usually wrong because the next round's surface is the prose the fix just added. This is prose only -- no production behaviour, no request rate, no assertion strength changes either way. Round 8 of an argued cap is precisely where review.md `two-round-cap` warns that further rounds find defects in the previous round's fix.
findings.title: A seventh stale-inventory sentence survives in the correctness suite, and THIS delta is what falsified it -- while backlog-done.md claims the form was deleted from the test comments
findings.detail:
theDELTASAfterTheCheckpointAreReplayed still opens with: `⚠️ THE OTHER HALF OF "newest checkpoint PLUS AT MOST K DELTAS", and every other test here is blind to it`. That is the same sentence FORM the commit body diagnoses six times -- an inventory of the other assertions in the file -- and it is now measurably false.

MEASURED, not argued. In my own copy of the staged bytes I inserted `if (hop.from() > 0) { return; }` at the top of ChainReplay.applyChain -- the exact mutant that comment names. Four tests in this file fail, not one:
  BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest.java:112  theDELTASAfterTheCheckpointAreReplayed   (its owner)
  BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest.java:261  aCheckpointSittingEXACTLYOnTheBarrierIsUsed   (request count)
  BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest.java:316  aRunOfBURNEDEpochsStillStopsAtTheCheckpointBehindThem   (request count)
  BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest.java:353  theBOUNDEDCrossingStillStopsAtTheSlotTheCONTINUENamed   (OFFSET -- added by this delta)
plus three in the sibling cost suite.

The two count-based failures pre-date this delta, so on the plainest reading the sentence was already stale at 87bc946fb5f9. But on the charitable reading -- 'blind to the tail-skip producing a WRONG ANSWER' -- it was true then and this delta is what broke it: the new test's assertion at line 353 is an offset, and under the tail-skip mutant the successor inherits 0 instead of 1, because the checkpoint at sequence 1 covers only the CONTINUE and the single real delta lives in the tail. Either way, the hunk that adds the new test created a fresh instance of the shape it was added alongside.

The second site is the commit's own evidence record. backlog-done.md's new M4.9 clause reads `AND THE STALE-INVENTORY FORM SURVIVED IN THE TWO DOCUMENTS CARRYING THE EVIDENCE after being deleted from the test comments`. The subordinate clause is false: the form was not deleted from the test comments, one instance remains at line 82, and the same delta falsified it. This is the identical failure the row itself names -- 'three of the six were created by the fix for the previous one and one by the other hunk of its own delta' -- occurring inside the sentence that announces the fix.

(Noted only, not a separate finding, because it pre-dates this delta and I passed it at round 7: line 43 of the same file still says `THE COST TESTS ABOVE ARE SATISFIED BY...` when the cost tests now live in another file, and the class javadoc's `it is satisfied by a recovery that reads nothing and is wrong` is now literally untrue of LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest, whose totals are exact -- a recovery that reads nothing issues fewer than 17 requests and fails them. The spirit -- the cost half does not check the answer -- still holds.)
findings.failure_scenario: A future session bounds a new replay path and needs to know which test protects 'newest checkpoint plus at most K deltas'. Line 82 tells it that theDELTASAfterTheCheckpointAreReplayed is the sole net, so a refactor that weakens or folds that one test looks safe by the comment's own logic -- while in fact three more tests in the same file and three in the sibling suite bite, and the reader has been given a false picture of where the coverage lives. Symmetrically, the next session greps backlog-done.md for the stale-inventory lesson, reads 'after being deleted from the test comments', and concludes the test comments are clean -- so the one that remains is the one nobody looks for. The remedy the row itself prescribes applies here: delete the clause rather than recount it, and drop 'and every other test here is blind to it' while keeping the durable half ('with K = 1 the newest checkpoint covers the whole chain, so a reader that skipped the tail entirely still produced the right answer'), which no edit elsewhere can falsify.
